title: The City That Couldn't Stop Dancing
sources: Britannica, 'dancing plague of 1518' (Strasbourg, July 1518; Frau Troffea began dancing in the street; hundreds danced; leaders decided more dancing was the cure; lasted about two months)
Public Domain Review, 'The Dancing Plague of 1518' (started 14 July; a stage built, musicians paid to play; dancers taken to the shrine of St Vitus)
National Geographic, 'dancing plague of 1518 Strasbourg choreomania' (around 400 people danced; cause still debated)
Popular Science (2025), 'The mysterious dancing plague that killed people in 1518' (as many as 400 by late August; council cleared the grain market, built a stage, hired musicians)

lines.text: A whole city once couldn't stop dancing.
a woman called Frau Troffea stepped into the street
lines.caps: a woman | called *Frau Troffea | stepped into | the *street

lines.text: and then her neighbours joined in.
By August, as many as four hundred people were dancing,

lines.text: so the city's leaders had a brilliant idea:

lines.text: They built a stage and hired a band,

lines.text: and it only made things worse.
To this day, nobody knows why it started.
